architecture.terrain_authority: The existing 1009x1009 reach-local Landscape remains the sole terrain rendering, collision, and height-query authority.
architecture.water_authority: The existing live cooked-field water remains the sole gameplay water rendering and raft-force authority; capture-only ribbon and foam actors remain hidden in play.
architecture.procedural_gap_fill: Eight dedicated non-colliding HISM actors add six rights-reviewed CC0 moss-rock morphology variants, short rainforest-floor cover, and a shrub transition. Every instance is grounded on Landscape height, slope screened, and placed outside the full visible-water and centerline-clearance boundary.
architecture.claims_boundary: The new dressing is deterministic procedural gap fill. It makes no exact Pacuare lithology, species, ecology, season, survey, hydraulic, bathymetry, or raft-force claim.

runtime_contract.shadow_policy: short ground cover self-shadow suppressed; shrubs and moss-rock analogs retain scene shading

matched_capture_metrics.scope: Two side-bank rectangles per fixed 1280x720 camera: x 0-419 and 860-1279, y 180-439.
matched_capture_metrics.green_dominant_definition: G > 1.16*R, G > 1.04*B, and G > 0.075 in normalized sRGB.
matched_capture_metrics.verdict: Retain as a bounded organic-bank improvement. Both views gain substantially more green bank cover and roughly double the measured small-scale edge structure without changing mean luminance materially. Increased near-black coverage and visibly procedural silhouettes prevent photoreal promotion.

validation.focused_runnable_map_gate: RaftSim.P4.RiverMapLoads.L_UpperHuacas passed 1/1, including eight shoreline actors and minimum instance-density checks
validation.visual_gate: matched fixed guide-seat and river-eye evidence retained as a technical improvement

remaining_photoreal_defects: Canopy crowns, trunks, shrub lobes, and ground-cover forms remain visibly procedural and repetitive rather than scanned or species-authentic rainforest assets.
The denser bank layer increases near-black coverage in both fixed views; lighting, material response, ambient occlusion, and silhouette quality still need environment-art refinement.
The 30 m source context and bounded procedural bank relief still produce broad smooth landforms without surveyed bank breaklines or production wet-bank microgeometry.
Generic moss-rock morphology donors make no Pacuare lithology claim; roots, leaf litter, deadwood, epiphytes, vines, wind response, wetness variation, and seasonal ecology remain incomplete.
Water remains optically thin with weak rapid foam, breaking-wave volume, spray, mist, rock-contact plumes, refraction, reflection, caustics, and riverbed transitions.
Cooked hydraulics remain unconverged and discharge, bathymetry, stationing, hazards, and guide line are not calibrated to observed Upper Huacas behavior.

geospatial review of exact stationing, planform, vertical datum, bank breaklines, higher-resolution terrain, rocks, and bathymetry
hydraulic calibration and convergence approval against observed Upper Huacas behavior across playable flow bands
ecology and environment-art approval of species, density, ground cover, geology, wet banks, lighting, and rainforest atmosphere
photoreal water/VFX plus raft, equipment, character, animation, and occlusion approval
desktop and VR target-hardware performance, collision, capsize, recovery, and complete-run gameplay acceptance
